title_question: Can I own a copy of an AI?
one_liner: Some AI models can be downloaded and run on your own hardware; these are open-weight models.

steps.title: Cloud AI sends your text away
steps.text: With cloud services, every message travels over the internet to a technology provider's remote data center for processing.

stage_state.description: Packets moving from laptop over internet to remote server racks.

steps.title: Open-weight models run locally
steps.text: With an open-weight release, you download the mathematical model file directly to your laptop or private server.

stage_state.description: Model weights stored inside local disk boundary with green security shield.

steps.title: Trade-offs: privacy versus hardware demands
steps.text: Running locally protects private files and provides complete control, but requires sufficient memory, manual setup, and self-managed security updates.

stage_state.description: Balance scale showing privacy and offline capability against RAM and configuration time.

steps.title: Read the community license terms
steps.text: Open weights is distinct from open source. Most creators provide the final weights while retaining custom usage terms and commercial thresholds.

stage_state.description: License document displaying acceptable use criteria and user threshold clauses.

analogy.text: Think of it like buying a finished cake from a bakery to take home. You own the cake sitting in your kitchen, but you did not receive the proprietary recipe, ingredient ratios, or kitchen ovens.
analogy.breaks: Some open science projects do release their training data and preparation scripts, and licenses vary substantially between community models.

myth.claim: Open-weight models are open source in the traditional software sense.
myth.reality: True open source provides the complete source code, training datasets, and unencumbered commercial rights. Open-weight models share the trained parameters under custom licenses.

seen_in: Ollama running lightweight models locally on a MacBook or Windows PC
LM Studio providing a private desktop chat interface
Private company servers hosting local models behind internal firewalls

persona_examples.student: Running a compact model on your laptop to summarize class notes without paying a monthly fee or needing Wi-Fi.
persona_examples.teacher: Evaluating student creative essays on an offline computer so student names do not leave school grounds.
persona_examples.entrepreneur: Hosting customer support intelligence on private cloud instances to maintain predictability over operational costs.
persona_examples.engineer_office: Analyzing confidential patent drafts and proprietary code repositories within an air-gapped corporate environment.

quiz.question: What is the primary difference between cloud AI and an open-weight model?
options: Cloud AI can only process English, while open-weight models understand any language
Cloud AI processes prompts on remote corporate servers, while open-weight models can execute on your own machine
Open-weight models cost millions of dollars for every user prompt
Cloud AI requires no internet connection
quiz.explanation: Open-weight models provide the model parameters directly so they can run on private local hardware.

quiz.question: Why might a healthcare clinic choose a local open-weight model instead of a public cloud chatbot?
options: Because local models have larger parameter counts than cloud models
To keep patient diagnostic records within local storage without transmitting data to third parties
Because local models make zero medical mistakes
Local models operate without consuming any electrical power
quiz.explanation: Local execution keeps sensitive records inside private network perimeters, avoiding third-party data processing.

quiz.question: Is the largest available model always the optimal choice for your computer?
options: Yes, larger models are superior for every scenario
No, larger models require substantial RAM and compute, whereas smaller quantized models run much faster and fit normal laptops
Yes, smaller models are unable to generate complete sentences
No, larger models are illegal to download
quiz.explanation: Hardware memory, speed, and energy costs dictate practical model selection. A compact model often satisfies daily tasks cleanly.

explain_back.prompt: Complete this sentence to prove you understand:
explain_back.template: An open-weight model lets you download and run the AI on your own hardware for privacy, but you must supply adequate memory and manage your own updates.

bullets: Model weights represent millions or billions of learned floating-point matrices (FP16 or BF16 precision).
Quantization compresses weights to lower precision (4-bit or 8-bit GGUF/AWQ formats), cutting RAM requirements by up to 75% with modest fidelity loss.
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures activate only a subset of total parameters per token, lowering computational latency.
Local runtimes (such as llama.cpp or vLLM) utilize hardware acceleration via Metal, CUDA, or Vulkan kernels.

code_panel.title: Running a Local Model via CLI
code_panel.code:
# Example: running an open-weight model locally using Ollama
ollama run llama3.2:3b

# Or using llama.cpp with a 4-bit quantized GGUF file
./main -m ./models/llama-3.2-3b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf \
       -p "Summarize this text locally:" \
       --threads 6 -ngl 33
